overrideReason: Attempts 1-2 failed on a genuine gap: the only test proving the RPC's real behavior was marked @pytest.mark.integration, deselected by pyproject.toml's default addopts, so the automated 'test' gate never actually executed it - only weaker offline substitutes (a mocked fetch call, a Python re-implementation of the SQL logic tested against itself) ran, proving nothing about the real function. Attempt 3's own diff fixed this correctly: tests/test_history_read.py now uses a real postgres fixture (matching the established, unmarked pattern already used by tests/test_persist_board.py, tests/test_board_read.py, etc. throughout this project) for every criterion provable against a throwaway schema, and reserves @pytest.mark.integration for only the one test that hits the real live PostgREST endpoint over HTTP. Attempt 3's automated verdict was 'verifier produced no parseable verdict' (0/6) - a verifier-tooling crash, not a real rejection, matching the same class of infra flake already seen this session for PRD-006's US-602. Verified directly instead: uv run pytest -q -m "not integration" tests/test_history_read.py passes 8/8 against a real throwaway Postgres schema, proving the bound, the ordering/tie-break, the single-vendor pin, and the empty-array case for real. The one remaining live PostgREST test failed with a 404 (PGRST202, function not found) because - exactly the same class of gap as PRD-008's US-807 - the history_read() migration had been written and tested against a throwaway schema but never applied to the real production database. Reviewed the migration directly: a single new read-only SQL function, no writes, no changes to any existing table/view, execute granted only to anon/authenticated. Applied to production with explicit owner authorization, reloaded PostgREST's schema cache, and the live test then passed. Full suite verified clean on current HEAD: uv run mypy ingest --strict clean, uv run ruff check clean, uv run pytest -q -m "not integration" 351 passed, npm --prefix web run typecheck clean, npm --prefix web test 55/55 passed.

results.note: tests/test_history_read.py::test_history_read_returns_at_most_the_requested_recent_live_or_backfill_points_newest_first passes against a real throwaway Postgres schema, proving the RPC bounds results to the requested point limit and returns origin in ('live','backfill') rows newest first.

tests/test_history_read.py::test_history_read_orders_by_source_timestamp_and_excludes_null_timestamp_absences and test_history_read_defines_id_desc_as_the_equal_timestamp_tie_break both pass, proving correct ordering, the id-desc tie-break, and that null-source_timestamp (UNAVAILABLE/ERROR) rows never enter the point series.
tests/test_history_read.py::test_history_read_pins_to_one_source_vendor_per_call passes, proving the RPC never interleaves two vendors' rows for the same indicator/asset.
tests/test_history_read.py::test_history_read_returns_empty_array_for_a_cell_with_no_rows passes, proving a cell with zero rows returns an empty JSON array, not an error.

tests/test_history_read.py::test_live_postgrest_history_read_for_a_real_cell_returns_one_bounded_array_under_the_default_row_cap re-run fresh after the migration was applied to production: PASSED against the real PostgREST endpoint, confirming the response stays under PostgREST's default row cap at this board's real point counts.
`uv run pytest -q -m "not integration"` re-run fresh against current HEAD: 351 passed, 66 deselected, exit 0. mypy --strict and ruff both clean.

note: All 6 criteria independently verified. This story's real path to done required fixing an integration-marker misclassification (present in attempts 1-2, corrected in attempt 3's own diff) and, once fixed, surfaced the second instance this PRD of a migration being written and tested but never applied to production - the same class of gap PRD-008's US-807 identified and fixed. Applied with explicit owner authorization, consistent with AGENTS.md's blast-radius policy for database migrations.
